text:
Jean-Gabriel Pageau turns 34 this week, and the Islanders are asking a lot of him: top-nine minutes on a team missing three regular forwards. He has eight points in 16 games, mostly assists, and one goal on a 5.3% shooting percentage that is almost certainly too low. The scoring will come back some.

The harder question is defense. The Islanders have been much worse at five on five with him on the ice than without him (about eight points of expected goal share), and Evolving-Hockey's numbers last season had opponents creating more against him than all but 4% of forwards. They also noted he was better than his goals: the chances were there, the finishing behind him wasn't.

What he still does well shows up in Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking: 73% of his exits leave the zone with possession, and he carries the puck in on 56% of his entries. That's useful hockey. Our range has him at 33 to 54 points over a full season. The fourth-round pick from his hometown Senators has had a long, productive career; how long he stays in this role depends on his line getting the puck out the other way.
headline: Pageau's role, and the cost
